channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: South Africa Defers Paris Club Bid, Turns to Borrowers’ Platform
item.description: South Africa told the Paris Club that it won’t seek full membership of the group of mostly rich-nation creditors, as it focuses on its involvement in a United Nations-backed coalition of borrower countries instead.
item.dc:creator: S'thembile Cele and Matthew Hill

item.title: Estonia Says Russia Behind Arson Attack on Defense Firm
item.description: Estonia’s government said with “full confidence” that Russian special services commissioned an August arson attack against a defense manufacturing facility in Tallinn.
item.dc:creator: Ott Tammik

item.title: China Offers Cheap Loans to Help State Firms Pay Overdue Bills
item.description: China has started offering low-cost funding to help local government-affiliated firms settle unpaid bills, according to people familiar with the matter, expanding efforts to mend corporate balance sheets and remove one of the biggest bottlenecks for investment.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Bardella Says He’s Suing Mediapart Over Antisemitic Allegations
item.description: Jordan Bardella, the head of the far-right National Rally, said he’s asked his lawyer to lodge a lawsuit after a French online news site published an article alleging he made a series of antisemitic comments over a decade ago.
item.dc:creator: Gaspard Sebag

item.title: Oil Climbs With Iran Pessimistic About Trump Deal Before US Midterms
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Global equities slid to a one-week low as surging oil prices and mounting bets on further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes drove Treasury yields to multi-year highs.
Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before US midterm elections in November, according to people familiar with the matter.
Today guests: Sunaina Sinha Haldea, Raymond James, Private Capital Advisory Global Head. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Malaysian Minister Vows to Quit When Najib Begins House Arrest
item.description: Malaysian Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said he will quit Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s cabinet once jailed former premier Najib Razak begins serving his house arrest granted under a conditional royal pardon.
item.dc:creator: Danial Azhar and Ram Anand

item.title: Oil Pushes Higher With Iran Pessimistic About US Deal
item.description: Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington before US midterm elections in November. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace has the latest developments. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Malaysia Begins Repatriating Group of Myanmar Nationals: AFP
item.description: Malaysia began repatriating a large group of Myanmar nationals on Tuesday, according to an Agence France-Presse report — the first phase of a plan to return 5,000 people to a country still engulfed in a civil war that has displaced millions.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan and Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: Iran Officials Pessimistic About US Deal Before Midterms
item.description: Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington before US midterm elections in November. Bloomberg's Jeff Mason has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House Releases Taxpayer-Funded Midterm Ads
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, AI Now Institute Senior Fellow for Economic and National Security Aya Ibrahim says Nvidia's new agent safety platform is a notable step, but cautions there is no one-size-fits-all solution to AI security risks, even as companies roll out new safeguards. Cook Political Report Founder and Contributor Charlie Cook says the midterm landscape has deteriorated sharply for Republicans in the past month as energy costs, tariffs and affordability concerns hit voters. Republican Congressman Mike Flood of Nebraska says diesel prices near record highs are putting pressure on Midwest farmers as harvest season gets underway. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Netanyahu, MBZ Discuss Ways to Bolster Ties During Visit to UAE
item.description: Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the United Arab Emirates where he held talks with the Gulf nation’s president, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, according to the Israeli premier’s office and the UAE’s state news agency.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: Rep. Flood: Diesel Prices 'Too High' for Farm Country
item.description: Republican Congressman Mike Flood of Nebraska says diesel prices near record highs are putting pressure on Midwest farmers as harvest season gets underway. The Republican Main Street Caucus chair says he wanted more from President Xi Jinping's visit and is pressing China to follow through on its US agricultural purchases. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pentagon Policy Chief Says NATO Allies Back Europe Defense Shift
item.description: As European capitals brace for US troop cuts, the Pentagon’s top policy official is telling lawmakers in Washington that allies are on board with a vision of “NATO 3.0” in which Europe maintains its own non-nuclear defense.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride

item.title: Burnham’s Vision for Britain Puts Pensions ‘Triple Lock’ in Play
item.description: Andy Burnham will pitch for honest political debate as the antidote to populism, as he reveals his plans for taking on thorny issues at his party’s annual conference.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain and Alex Wickham

item.title: Iran Officials Pessimistic About US Deal Before Midterms
item.description: Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before US midterm elections in November, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Fiona MacDonald, Salma El Wardany, Alex Wickham and Samy Adghirni

item.title: Trump Criticizes UK’s Release of Airbase Suspects Amid Probe
item.description: President Donald Trump criticized the release on bail of five men held over an alleged terror plot against a Royal Air Force base used by the US for strikes against Iran, as British police continue to investigate foreign links to the incident.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Trump Touts Giant Essar Steel Plant for Battleground State
item.description: US President Donald Trump said a company owned by India’s Essar Group will build a $15 billion steel plant in Iowa, a crucial midterm battleground state where voter dissatisfaction over the economy has hurt Republicans.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: India’s Commerce Minister Heads to US as Trade Talks Drag On
item.description: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal will hold bilateral meetings with his US counterpart during a visit this week as the two sides seek to finalize an interim trade deal.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Srivastava

item.title: China Signals New Stimulus Measures to Support Slowing Economy
item.description: China has given its strongest signal yet that it will move with greater urgency to counter a deepening slowdown, as the government promised to introduce new measures to support the economy and study policies to stabilize the reeling property market.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Bessent Taps Market Strategist Zervos as Treasury Adviser
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tapped David Zervos, a longtime market and policy analyst at investment bank Jefferies, as an adviser with an unspecified role.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy and Denitsa Tsekova
